abla\log f + span\{1,v\}$) derived for the continuous problem does not hold for (djko_p2); Proposition prop:added-4(i) is vacuous (there is no optimizer); Algorithm algorithm_jko minimizes an unbounded objective; and assumption (A.1) of Theorem thm_opt_conv ($\ell_* > -\infty$) fails for this loss. The same bump construction shows the particle objective (djko_p) is unbounded below, defeating prop:added-3 as well.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must make the entropy term coercive relative to the action, e.g., retain the inner-time integral of the action in the training objective (continuous-in-inner-time training) or add a penalty controlling $\nabla u$ at the particles, and then re-derive the discrete optimality conditions; flipping the sign or re-linearizing the one-step entropy term does not fix it (the exact-log-det one-step variant is also unbounded below).
issues.overall_effect: The defining optimization problem of the proposed particle method is ill-posed (infimum $-\infty$, no minimizer). The advertised exact discrete entropy dissipation and unconditional stability (prop:added-4, abstract, introduction) are unsupported as stated; the SGD convergence guarantee (thm_opt_conv) does not apply because its infimum assumption fails; and the trained field is not characterized by the score relation (opt_u1).
issues.title: The fully discrete JKO loss (djko_p2) is unbounded below, so the minimization defining the method has no solution
issues.why_classification: The central algorithmic object of the paper is ill-posed and its main advertised guarantee (exact entropy decay via minimization) is withdrawn; every supported repair requires changing the loss or adding a new construction rather than a local fix.

issues.failure_explanation: Summing the per-$q$ estimate over $q=1,\dots,Q$ ($Q=N/B$) requires $\sum_q q\sum_{p\le q}a_p \le \frac{Q^2}{2}\Delta$, $\sum_q q \le \frac{Q^2}{2}$ and $\sum_q q^2 \le \frac{Q^3}{3}$. In fact $\sum_q q\sum_{p\le q}a_p \le \frac{Q(Q+1)}{2}\Delta$, $\sum_q q = \frac{Q(Q+1)}{2} > \frac{Q^2}{2}$ and $\sum_q q^2 = \frac{Q(Q+1)(2Q+1)}{6} > \frac{Q^3}{3}$. The displayed intermediate inequality therefore understates the right-hand side (positive terms were dropped from an upper bound), and the absorption step using $\alpha_k \le \frac{1}{L\sqrt3}$ is insufficient because the true coefficient is $\frac{3\alpha_k^2L^2}{2}(1+\frac{B}{N})$. The stated bound on $\Delta$ is unproved as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redo the summation with the correct bounds ($\frac{Q(Q+1)}{2}\le Q^2$, $\frac{Q(Q+1)(2Q+1)}{6}\le \frac{Q^3}{3}+\frac{Q^2}{2}+\frac{Q}{6}$) and re-derive the constants and the step-size condition in sgd_lemma1 and thm_opt_conv; a small reoptimization of constants preserves the lemma's form.
issues.overall_effect: The epoch-drift bound in the shuffling-SGD analysis is unproved as stated, and Theorem thm_opt_conv, which combines this lemma with sgd_lemma2, inherits the gap.
issues.title: Invalid summation bounds in the proof of Lemma sgd_lemma1
issues.why_classification: The proof contains a concrete false summation inequality, but the lemma's form and the convergence rate survive after a contained reoptimization of constants and the step-size condition; no new proof architecture is needed.
